en.intro: I work in **Data & AI at Edenred**, with technical leadership responsibilities in applied AI, and **own LensPart**. My specialty connects images, visual representations and applications that support operational decisions.
en.intro2: At **TK Elevator**, I developed **SnapSupply from concept to deployment**. My earlier experience in industrial maintenance, production and automation connects AI engineering with the conditions systems face in the field.

areas.title: Computer vision
areas.text: Image-to-description validation and visual recognition, with attention to image quality, difficult examples and the limits of automated decisions.

areas.title: Multimodal AI
areas.text: Connecting images, context and model outputs to operational needs. Making evaluation criteria and integration dependencies explicit.

areas.title: Technical delivery
areas.text: Aligning technical and business teams around requirements, UAT, application integration, documentation and environment promotion.

en.notes_intro: Independent artifacts for inspecting the engineering approach. The runnable demo uses synthetic data; the notes are engineering references.

notes.title: Evaluation lab
notes.label: RUNNABLE DEMO
notes.text: Measure accepted-decision quality, coverage and human-review rate together. Includes a zero-dependency evaluator, synthetic fixtures and tests.

notes.title: Visual validation
notes.label: REFERENCE DESIGN
notes.text: A compact design note on inputs, decision thresholds, difficult examples and the boundary between an automated decision and human review.

notes.title: From validation to integration
notes.label: DELIVERY NOTE
notes.text: A practical outline for acceptance criteria, environment promotion, application integration and meaningful operational monitoring.

principles: Define the operational decision and the people who depend on it.
Consider variation in image quality, context and real usage conditions.
Discuss quality, latency, cost and the need for human review together.
Keep assumptions, dependencies and acceptance criteria understandable to the team.
en.background: I started building for the web before specializing in AI. My background spans industrial maintenance, solar energy projects, production and automation, followed by postgraduate training in **Data Science & AI (2025)**. Today I bring those operational and software perspectives to enterprise AI delivery.
en.closing: I am interested in the practical questions that make AI useful: what should the system decide, how do we know it works, and how does it fit into the operation?
